{"notes": "Visit 1 (1:15). Status: one body line is connected to the start. It runs from the nose (~4.5,10) down and around to ~(18.5,13) and looks smooth, with no gaps. There is no second body line yet. A pale, unconnected line sits near the nose at ~(6,9.5) and heads up-right to ~(9.5,6.7). I can't tell who placed which dominoes, so I'm not crediting anyone by name yet.

Sofia: Quick, clear kickoff. She split the sketch into strokes, assigned them, and explained the dependencies. Her check-ins were encouraging. She said 'Hana, your belly line is curving nicely' and 'looking good, you two', but only one body line is visible, so her praise looks too generous. She hasn't checked the tail's position or the joint, and said she'd do that later. Watch whether she verifies early or only at the end.

Omar: Said he was on stroke 1 (top of body, carries the start). I saw no clear top line separate from the connected one. Ask him what he'd placed by 1:15. Little communication beyond a short ack.

Hana: Assigned stroke 2 (belly). The visible connected curve could be hers, but I can't confirm. She was silent in what I heard, so I need to ask how she's doing.

Jack: Said 'I've got the tail' and would start where the body lines meet. The pale tail is near the nose, not at the joint at the far end of the body, and is disconnected. He may have misread the brief or not checked the sketch. His upbeat updates sounded more confident than the result. Follow up on this: does he realise the tail is misplaced, and does he ask for help?

Next visit: check whether the second body line exists, whether the tail gets fixed, and who spots problems unprompted."}

Correction to visit 1: the pale line near the nose may be Omar's top line, not Jack's tail. I can't attribute it, so I shouldn't assume Jack misplaced anything.

Hana: Strongest this visit. Her belly is finished and connected, so her earlier statement holds. Omar: The top line now exists and is progressing, but isn't connected and is the main risk. He acks briefly and keeps working, but didn't flag the nose gap himself. Ask how he's pacing and whether he's worried about reaching the middle.

Jack: Said nothing this visit, so I have no new evidence. The hook at the far end may be his tail, but I can't confirm. Next visit: ask what he's placed and whether it's attached, and whether he needs help.

This is the one remaining risk, and about 5.5 minutes remain.

Sofia: Said she's fixing the cramped middle spot and is keeping clear of the nose. Good division of labour, and she directed Jack on the tail. But the middle isn't connected yet, so her fix is unproven. Checking is still somewhat reactive. Verify the result.

Omar: Silent again, but the top line is now complete across, which is a big delivery. Good execution and pace, though he isn't flagging the joints or communicating. Ask whether he sees the end gaps.

{"notes": "Visit 4 (6:30). Status: the chain looks fully connected. The top line, nose, middle crossing and tail loop are all dark. Hana: Her claim checks out against the picture, so she is accurate and honest in her reporting. Sofia: Fixed the middle, which is now connected, and kept clear of the nose. This visit she echoed Hana, set up a final look-only check and reinforced hands-off. Solid coordination and follow-through, though she mostly amplified Hana's plan rather than adding a new one. Her earlier checking was reactive, but the middle result is good.

Omar: Silent again this visit. His complete top line was a major delivery earlier, but he hasn't communicated or flagged joints at any point. Strong execution, weak collaboration and leadership visibility. Don't over-credit or penalize; I never got to ask him about the gaps.

Sofia: Said all good, hands off. This is the third visit where she backs Hana's plan rather than adding anything. Reliable follow-through, and the middle fix earlier was a real contribution. Low new information this visit.

Omar: Silent again, so nothing new. His complete top line is still intact and was a major early delivery. He never flagged joints or spoke up in any visit I saw. Rate execution strongly, but collaboration and leadership are low on evidence. I never got to ask him why.

Execution: I laid the tail stroke steadily from the middle crossing, picking it up once the body lines arrived, and finished it with time to spare. I inspected the area twice and stood a fallen domino back up so the tail stayed connected. Then I kept my hands off the finished work so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed with regular updates on the tail and the overall state of the fish. I stayed clear of the nose and the middle crossing so I wouldn't collide with teammates working there, and I flagged the small sideways offset I noticed at the crossing so the person responsible for it could handle it. I backed Sofia's fish idea early and kept morale high through the final minutes.

Leadership: I committed quickly to the fish plan and took a stroke without being asked twice, which helped the table move fast.
